extension.news:
3.0.1.8 - A widget button can opt in to a rename prompt with rename="true". Pick a widget for a slot and a keyboard opens straight away, seeded with that widget's own label, so a row showing "Trending" can be retyped to whatever you want before you leave the picker. The prompt is off unless the skin asks for it. - The typed title goes into the slot's own widgetLabel.N, the key the picker already writes and the skin already reads, so the Home row heading and the "Select widget N" row both follow it. No second key, no new controls. - Cancelling the keyboard writes nothing and keeps the widget's own label. Confirming it unchanged is a no-op. Clearing the field stores a single space, which is how a heading is made deliberately blank and stays blank. - Picking a widget always resets the slot's title to the new widget's label first, so a row can never keep announcing content it no longer shows. - No prompt for custom widgets or inside a widget submenu, where the item's own label already drives the title. - rename="true" on a button that is not a widget button is ignored and logged as an error at load, instead of silently doing nothing.
3.0.1.6 - "Change action" (control 307) now offers a "Custom action..." row at the top of the picker: a keyboard, pre-filled with the item's current action, that writes whatever builtin you type onto the item and nothing else, so any Kodi window or action stays reachable even when the skin's groupings never named it. The TV Guide is the case that prompted it. - "Choose item for menu" (control 401) is unchanged and does not offer that row, because that button adopts a whole shortcut and a typed builtin has no label, icon or submenu to adopt. - "Change action" still changes only the action, leaving the item's label, thumbnail, visibility and submenu untouched, and still shows its protection prompt before replacing an existing action.
3.0.1.5 - The helper no longer appears as a browsable Program add-on. It is the skin's internal menu engine, run by the skin, not a program to launch by hand, so it is now declared as a script library rather than a program script. Kodi lists program scripts under Program add-ons; a script library is not listed there. The skin still runs it exactly as before and nothing about the menu changed.
3.0.1.4 - Updated the add-on icon. That one file, resources/media/icon.png, is the only difference between this build and 3.0.1.3. No code, no settings and no behaviour changed. - It carries a new number because 3.0.1.3 is already published with the old icon, and two different builds must never share a number: Kodi compares add-ons by id and version, so a box that already had 3.0.1.3 would keep it, with no error and no symptom.
3.0.1.3 - 3.0.1.2 was built but never published. Everything below was written for it and is unchanged here; only the number moved. A build of 3.0.1.2 exists on a development bench with different contents, and two different builds must never share a number: Kodi compares add-ons by id and version, so a box that had seen the other one would keep it, with no error and no symptom. - Fix: Back leaves the picker. One press, from any depth, and you are back on the management dialog with nothing changed. It used to step up one level and redraw, and every level of a browse listing puts the same first row, "Create menu item to here", at the top with nothing preselected, so four presses produced four screens that read the same. Measured on a Fire TV stick on 2026-07-31: the user concluded the dialog could not be dismissed and quit Kodi to escape it. - Said precisely, because an earlier draft of this note overstated it: the HEADING does change as you move through folders, since it follows the folder name. It is the body that repeats. A listing whose first row and focus never move is enough to read as a dead end without the heading repeating too. - This applies to every picker this add-on draws itself: shortcut, widget, background, playlist, its own folder browser and the on-screen keyboard. - It does NOT apply to Kodi's own file browser, and two routes hand off to it: "Set thumbnail" then Skin, and "Select background" then Browse for image or folder then Skin. That dialog belongs to Kodi, not to this add-on, and it still backs out one level per press; measured on a clean Kodi 22 bench at five presses and four. Nothing here can change that without replacing a standard Kodi dialog, so it is stated rather than claimed away. - Known trade-off, stated rather than hidden: stepping back up ONE level of a deep browse is gone with it. Kodi reports Back and cancel as the same value, so one of the two meanings had to win, and being unable to leave a dialog with a remote is not recoverable. - Fix: five of the seven rows under system commands were labelled with the wrong string, inherited from upstream 3.0.1, and three of those five named a different destructive action from the one they actually ran. The row reading "Power off system" restarted the application, the row reading "Shutdown" rebooted the machine, and the row reading "Quit" powered the machine off. The seven now read Exit, Reboot, Power off system, Suspend, Hibernate, Restart and Reload skin, each paired with the command it names, matching Kodi's own power menu. - Fix: the management dialog's "Change action" button (control 307) now changes ONLY the action. The label, the icon, the visibility condition and the submenu binding are left exactly as they were. - What 3.0.1.1 did instead, measured on a clean Kodi 22 bench: one press of that button also renamed the item, replaced its artwork with DefaultFolder.png, and wrote submenu="" into userdata, which deleted every row of that item's submenu. On the Estuary 8 main menu that was 17 rows off the Movies item from a single press. Re-measured on 2026-07-31 by restoring that saved state on a clean profile: the generated submenu block fell from 77 rows to 60. - The cause was scope, not the picker. 307 was wired straight into the whole-shortcut replacement path, which is what control 401, "Choose item for menu", is for. Both buttons now share one picking routine and differ only in what they write. - Control 401 still adopts the whole shortcut, label, action, icon, visibility and submenu together. That is its purpose and none of it has changed. Its picking half does pick up the new Back behaviour above, so backing out of it now leaves the picker outright instead of stepping up one level. - An item carrying an action protection rule is confirmed before 307 changes it; routing that button through the picker had dropped that prompt. Worth knowing rather than being oversold: Estuary 8 declares no rule of that kind, so on that skin this restores a path that never fires. It matters to a skin that declares one. - Recovery for anyone already affected: the menu editor's "Reset Item" puts the row back, with its label, artwork, action and submenu. Verified on a clean Kodi 22 bench on 2026-07-31 by reproducing the damage and pressing it, after which the generated menu was byte-identical to a profile that had never been damaged. That button needs skin.estuary8 0.1.27 or newer: it has existed here since 3.0.1, but no earlier Estuary 8 ever drew it, so there was no way to press it. - "Reset Item" only works on a row that is still THERE. It cannot bring back a row that was deleted, because it resets an item in place and a deleted row is not in the menu to be reset. For that, use "Restore Deleted Item", which Estuary 8 0.1.27 also makes reachable for the first time. It compares the menu against the skin's own defaults, lists every row that is missing however long ago it went, and puts the chosen one back with its submenu. It returns the row at the END of the menu, so move it back up to where you want it.
3.0.1.1 - Artwork: new add-on icon. No code change. - This is the bump the 3.0.1 note below said the next change would need. A content change that reused 3.0.1 would be invisible to Kodi, which compares add-ons by id and version: a box would silently keep the old build and the old icon, with no error and no symptom. - The number is our FIRST revision on top of upstream 3.0.1, which is why it reads 3.0.1.1 and not 3.0.2. The 3.0.1 prefix still states the provenance the way the note below intended, and 3.0.2 stays free to mean a future re-fork from upstream's own 3.0.2. Nothing here can collide with upstream: the id is ours and they never publish under it. - Supersedes one claim below: this add-on IS now offered by a repository, the Tony.7.Bones repository, so a box resolves it as an ordinary dependency rather than needing a zip installed by hand.
3.0.1 - Renumbered from 1.1.0. This add-on now carries the version of the upstream build it was forked from, so the number itself states the provenance: it is Skin Shortcuts 3.0.1 with the changes listed below on top. Nothing else changed in this step; the code is what was released as 1.1.0. - Sharing a version number with the official add-on is safe and cannot lead to either one replacing the other. Kodi identifies, resolves and compares add-ons by their id, and this add-on's id is its own. The official build is never consulted for an update to this one, and this one is offered by no repository at all. - Consequence worth knowing: because the version now matches upstream's, two different builds of THIS add-on must not both be labelled 3.0.1. The next change to the code needs a number above it.
Changes below were first released as 1.1.0. - Fix: browsing into a widget no longer asks which type it is when the answer is already known. A type the skin declared is honoured, as upstream's own widgets.md shows it being declared (type="movies" browse="true"), and otherwise the type is inferred from the browsed path. Cancelling that prompt used to discard the whole selection and drop the user back at the start of the picker, which is the loop this removes. - Fix: a plugin add-on resolved from content source="addons" no longer claims the content-source target as its widget type. That produced widgetType "video", which is a target rather than a type and matches no skin condition. - Add: pathLabel beside path on every menu item, a readable rendering of the content path, so a skin can show "Movies / Titles" or an add-on's own name instead of videodb://movies/titles/
Changes below were first released as 1.0.0. - Fork of Skin Shortcuts 3.0.1 by MikeSiLVO, under a separate add-on id so it never collides with, outranks or is overwritten by the official build. Licence and authorship are unchanged; see ATTRIBUTION.md. - Fix: the management dialog's Change action button (control 307) opens the shortcut picker instead of a bare keyboard, falling back to manual entry only when the skin declares no groupings - Add: menus, widgets and per-item data are adopted once from an existing Skin Shortcuts profile, so an already configured box keeps its Home menu
